attrs.evidence: Reproduced. Privacy currencies are real-valued (ρ = Δ²/2σ²), so a real-valued instantiation needs rational or fixed-point amounts, or a tolerance in CB2. NOT FIXED in this round: it is a representation change to a shipped kernel and it was not required by any gate this round set. ROUND 3 narrowed the representation question and rejected one proposed answer. SOUND: exact rationals when the currency is rational; fixed-point with cost rounded UP and cap rounded DOWN is conservative for additive comparisons and never undercounts, while float64 admits unsoundly at a sub-resolution cap. NOT SOUND AS A UNIVERSAL ANSWER: "exact rationals" does not cover nonlinear conversions — log, sqrt, a minimum over RDP orders, PLD discretization — each of which needs its own directed/interval soundness argument. AND CB2 MUST KEEP ITS BRIDGE MEANING: replacing it with "add is associative and commutative" would demote an operational law (charging a pipeline sequentially has the same resource effect as charging the composed cost) into an algebra law about the representation. Keep both, do not substitute one for the other.
attrs.gap: Deliberately left open and recorded rather than silently fixed. Anyone instantiating #27b with a real-valued currency hits this first.
attrs.review_focus: CB2 as property-tested uses strict integer equality and privacy currencies are real-valued. This is the first thing anyone instantiating 27b with a real currency will hit, and the representation choice is entangled with LED-ACCOUNTANT-ALGEBRA.
attrs.statement: CB2, as literally property-tested, uses strict equality on integers and fails on real-valued costs (0.1 + 0.2 + 0.3 ≠ 0.6 in binary floating point).
